Network.description:
Radio links between the vehicles and the ground (task P2-T02).

With this section every vehicle talks to the ground station and to the other vehicles over
its own radio link, shaped by a profile (latency, jitter, loss, reordering, rate), while its
bridge and the run's recorder reach it unimpaired; the timeline changes a link with
`link.set`, `link.drop` and `link.restore`. Without it the vehicles share the run's network
as they always did.

profile.description: Profile of every vehicle's link: a preset (`wifi_good`, `lte_rural`, `rf_900mhz_5km`) or a name under `profiles`.
profile.title: Profile

links.description: Profile of a vehicle's link instead of `profile` (vehicle name to profile).
links.title: Links

profiles.description: Profiles of this scenario, by name.
profiles.title: Profiles

verify.description: What a link whose measured latency is not within 10 % of its profile does: nothing, a warning, or fails the run.
verify.title: Verify

the end of the timeline. The evidence is the closest sample and the final pose.

Time.description:
The clock of the run (ADR-0006, task P2-T04; docs/reference/time.md).

`sim`: the simulator free-runs at the target real-time factor and the timeline is scheduled
on the wall clock. `realtime`: the real-time factor is pinned to 1.0 and the drift between
simulation time and the wall clock is monitored over the timeline, warned about and, with
`on_drift: fail`, fails the run past `max_drift_s`. `lockstep`: the simulator advances in
steps of `step_s` only once every vehicle has acknowledged the previous one (a clock agent
in each vehicle's network namespace), the engine holds it at every timeline due time and
while an event is being started, and the timeline and the assertions run in simulation time.

mode.description: `sim`: simulated time on /clock at the target real-time factor; `realtime`: real-time-locked (RTF 1.0, drift monitored); `lockstep`: stepped, the simulator waiting for every vehicle's acknowledgement.
mode.title: Mode

rtf.description: Target real-time factor (absent: the world's own setting). In `realtime` mode it is 1.0; in `lockstep` mode it is the pace cap of a step (1.0 by default).
rtf.title: Rtf

tolerance.description: Allowed deviation of the measured real-time factor from the target over a metrics window (counted in the record; a `clock.drift` warning in realtime mode).
tolerance.title: Tolerance

max_drift_s.description: `realtime`: the drift between simulation time and the wall clock tolerated over the timeline (simulation seconds minus wall-clock seconds).
max_drift_s.title: Max Drift S

on_drift.description: `realtime`: what a drift past `max_drift_s` does: fail the run or warn.
on_drift.title: On Drift

step_s.description: `lockstep`: simulation seconds per step (a multiple of the world's physics step).
step_s.title: Step S

ack_timeout_s.description: `lockstep`: wall-clock seconds a vehicle may take to acknowledge a step before the run fails.
ack_timeout_s.title: Ack Timeout S

timeout_s.description: Wall-clock budget of the run once every vehicle is ready.
timeout_s.title: Timeout S

Time.title: Time

TopicRate.description:
A ROS topic keeps publishing at a rate.

Measured over a sliding window once `after_s` has passed after the timeline starts; fails
at the first window below `min_hz` (or above `max_hz`) and at the end of the timeline if
nothing was received.

name.title: Name

topic.description: The topic (relative to the vehicle's namespace when `vehicle` is given).
topic.title: Topic

vehicle.description: The vehicle the topic belongs to.
vehicle.title: Vehicle

min_hz.description: Lowest acceptable rate over a window.
min_hz.title: Min Hz

after_s.description: Grace period after the timeline starts before windows count.
after_s.title: After S

TopicRate.title: TopicRate

TopicValue.description:
A condition over a field of a ROS topic's messages.

`condition` is an expression over `value`, the field of each message (`value < 1.5`,
`abs(value) <= 0.2`, `0 < value and value < 2`); `mode` says whether every message after
`after_s` must satisfy it (`always`, fails at the first that does not, passes at `within_s`
or the end) or one must (`eventually`, passes at the first that does, fails at `within_s`
or the end). `after_s` and `within_s` make a window: "the vehicle is stopped from 12 s to
27 s" is `mode: always`, `after_s: 12s`, `within_s: 27s`.

name.description: Assertion name: lower case, digits and underscores.
name.title: Name

topic.description: The topic (relative to the vehicle's namespace when `vehicle` is given).
topic.title: Topic

vehicle.description: The vehicle the topic belongs to.
vehicle.title: Vehicle

after_s.description: Grace period after the timeline starts before messages count.
after_s.title: After S

anyOf.description: Seconds, or a duration such as '90s', '1m30s' or '2h'.

within_s.description: End of the window: the deadline of `eventually`, the end of `always` (absent: the end of the timeline).
within_s.title: Within S

Vehicle.description:
One vehicle of the scenario.

In a fleet every vehicle has its own `namespace`: its Gazebo topics, its ROS topics (the TF
topics included, Nav2's multi-robot convention) and its nodes live under it, so nothing of
one vehicle reaches another. `frame_prefix` is for a stack that keeps one shared `/tf` tree
instead and tells its frames apart by name (REP 105); it is passed to the spawn, the bridge
and the vehicle's launch (`runtime.entrypoint.launch.frame_prefix_arg`).

name.title: Name

namespace.title: Namespace

VideoOutput.description:
A video of the run from a camera of the world (issue #46).

The camera is a `<sensor type="camera">` of the world file with Gazebo's
`CameraVideoRecorder` system attached; the runner starts the recording when the timeline
starts, stops it when the timeline ends and copies the file into the run directory.

camera.description: Name of the world's camera sensor (its recorder service is `/<camera>/record_video`).
camera.title: Camera

VideoOutput.title: VideoOutput

When.description:
A condition of the run that triggers a timeline entry the first time it holds.

Either a field of a ROS topic's messages (`topic`, `field`, like a `topic_value`
assertion) or a `metric` of the run: `sim_time` (the simulator's clock, in seconds; the
one trigger in simulation time), `rtf` (the measured real-time factor), or the vehicle's
ground-truth `x`, `y`, `z`, `yaw` (radians) and `distance_to` a `target` placement
(metres). `condition` is an expression over `value` (`value > 0.3`, `value < 2.0`).
`vehicle` says whose topic or ground truth; it defaults to the entry's vehicle.

topic.description: A ROS topic (relative to the vehicle's namespace when there is a vehicle).
topic.title: Topic

metric.description: A metric of the run instead of a topic: `sim_time`, `rtf`, or the vehicle's `x`, `y`, `z`, `yaw`, `distance_to`.
metric.title: Metric

target.description: The placement `distance_to` measures to (in the world).

vehicle.description: The vehicle (default: the entry's) the topic or metric is of.
vehicle.title: Vehicle
